title: ATOMS: ALMA Three-millimeter Observations of Massive Star-forming regions - IV. Radio recombination lines and evolution of star formation efficiencies
question: Can millimeter radio recombination line H40alpha trace UC HII regions and star formation rates in Galactic massive clumps, how do bolometric luminosities correlate with CS J=2-1 and HC3N J=11-10 molecular line luminosities, and how do formed OB stars affect star formation efficiency?

recipe.goal: Extract compact objects and measure sizes and line fluxes
recipe.method: Fit 2D elliptical Gaussians to the integrated intensity maps of CS J=2-1, HC3N J=11-10, and H40alpha to obtain offsets, aspect ratios, effective radii, peak flux densities, and total velocity-integrated flux densities; sum multiple objects per targeted source to obtain overall clump properties.
key_parameters: R_eff = sqrt(a * b), aspect ratio = a / b where a and b are deconvolved semi-major and semi-minor sizes

recipe.goal: Derive ionized gas properties (ionization rate Q0, electron density ne, and ionized gas mass Mion) from H40alpha
recipe.method: Compute H40alpha line luminosity from integrated flux and distance, then calculate recombination/ionization rate Q0, electron density ne, and ionized gas mass Mion using Case B recombination equations.
assumptions: T_e = 10^4 K and n_e = 10^4 cm^-3 for excitation efficiency, weak maser effects, Case B recombination in steady state (Q0 = R_rec), helium ionization neglected (n_p = n_e), mean mass per proton mu = 1.27 for 27% helium

recipe.goal: Calculate molecular line luminosities and fit Lbol-L'mol scaling relations
recipe.method: Convert velocity-integrated fluxes of CS J=2-1 and HC3N J=11-10 into molecular line luminosities L'mol using Solomon et al. (1997) Equation 1, and perform linear least squares fits in log-log space against Lbol.
assumptions: Distances taken from Liu et al. (2020a) and Lbol from SED integration (Faúndez et al. 2004; Urquhart et al. 2018)

recipe.goal: Compare Lbol-to-L'mol ratios across Galactocentric distance and between clumps with and without H40alpha emission
recipe.method: Plot Lbol/L'mol against Galactocentric distance RGC and perform Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests on the log(Lbol/L'mol) distributions of clumps with and without H40alpha emission across six molecular tracers (CS 2-1, HC3N 11-10, H13CN 1-0, H13CO+ 1-0, HCN 1-0, HCO+ 1-0).

recipe.goal: Estimate star formation rates (SFRbol and SFRH40alpha) and gas depletion times
recipe.method: Calculate SFRbol from Lbol and SFRH40alpha from H40alpha line luminosity; compare SFRH40alpha/SFRbol for sources with SFR >= 5 Msun Myr^-1; compute ionized-to-molecular mass ratios Mion/Mmol and gas depletion times t_dep = Mass/SFR.
key_parameters: log(SFR / Msun Myr^-1) = log(Lbol / ergs s^-1) - 37.41; SFR(H40alpha) / (Msun Myr^-1) = 3.008 x 10^-3 * [L(H40alpha) / (Jy km/s kpc^2)]; threshold SFR >= 5 Msun Myr^-1
assumptions: Well-sampled Kroupa & Weidner (2003) IMF and steady-state massive star birth/death for SFR >= 5 Msun Myr^-1 (Lbol >= 10^4.5 Lsun); molecular clump masses taken from single-dish dust continuum in Liu et al. (2020a)

score_reason: The analytical equations for line luminosities, ionized gas properties, and SFRs are explicitly and thoroughly documented in Appendices A and B, and full measurement tables are provided in online supplementary material. However, raw-to-image cube generation is deferred to earlier ATOMS papers and velocity integration ranges for the moment-0 maps are not specified.
rediscovery_reason: ALMA project 2019.1.00685.S is public, the paper provides explicit analytical equations in Appendices A and B and full source catalogs online, and the main results are clear numeric scaling slopes, KS tests, and summary statistics.
